children: Alphabet Inc (GOOGL, Financials), the parent company of Google, is increasing its AI presence in Europe by directly delivering more of its research tools to academics.
Google DeepMind and Google Cloud are providing 200 European researchers with access to cutting-edge AI models and $3 million in computing credits.

The program contains tools like AlphaFold 3 for molecular research, AlphaGenome for genomics, WeatherNext for forecasting, AlphaEvolve for algorithm development and AlphaEarth Foundations for Earth observation.
From Alphabet's perspective, $3 million is hardly a huge financial commitment. More intriguing is the strategic value.
Giving researchers early access to Google's models and cloud infrastructure might cement such tools into scientific processes, creating a long-term demand for Google Cloud.

It also provides Alphabet another option to show that its AI goal goes beyond consumer products like Gemini. The program is aimed to speed up scientific discovery and improve research competitiveness in Europe, Google says.
The challenge for investors is whether projects like these eventually convert into greater cloud usage and better acceptance of Google's own AI capabilities.
It will be interesting to see which European research teams join the program, and whether Google extends the effort beyond the first 200 participants.

title: Google Is Turning Scientific AI Into a European Cloud Growth Strategy
